newsitem.title: UK: Overhaul of UK social security needed-MORI survey.
newsitem.headline: Overhaul of UK social security needed-MORI survey.

text.p: A majority of Britons want to see bigger pensions, higher unemployment benefit and child benefit clearly targeted to the worst off, a survey showed on Monday.
The survey, conducted for Readers' Digest by MORI, said three quarters of respondents think pensions are too low and 57 percent believe unemployment benefit payments are too mean.
Some 49 percent said child benefit should be targeted toward those with the lowest income, with 44 percent backing its current univeral status.
"With social security spending at 92 billion pounds a year and rising, the welfare state is destined for either major overhaul or meltdown," said Russell Twisk of Readers' Digest.
"Our survey proves there is widespread public awareness of the crisis and must be a powerful spur for political action."
The survey also found two thirds of the respondents thought the unemployed should do community or other work to qualify for unemployment benefit.
It also found three quarters favoured tax concessions for women who stay at home to care for children.
MORI surveyed 2,031 poeple aged 15 and over between July 22 and 28. Data was then weighed to the known national profile.
